keyQuotes: It shatters the heavy-compute narrative, making high-quality inpainting accessible on consumer-grade and edge devices.
Moebius achieves this using less than 2% of the parameters (0.22B vs. 11.9B) while delivering a >15× acceleration in total inference time.
Rather than blindly scaling up, Moebius answers a fundamental question: Can a model be smarter, lighter, and faster when the task is explicitly defined?

mainPoints.explanation: Through synergistic architecture-distillation optimization, Moebius rivals FLUX.1-Fill-Dev and SD3.5 Large-Inpainting across 6 benchmarks, despite using less than 2% of the parameters.
With 26 ms per step on a single GPU, Moebius delivers a total runtime acceleration of over 15× compared to 10B-level models, making high-quality inpainting accessible on consumer hardware.
mainPoints.point: 15× inference speedup enables real-time or edge deployment.

mainPoints.explanation: The Local-λ Mix Interaction block condenses spatial context and global semantic priors into fixed-size linear matrices, bypassing the quadratic complexity of standard self-/cross-attention.
mainPoints.point: LλMI block eliminates quadratic attention overhead.

mainPoints.explanation: Operating strictly in latent space, the distillation aligns intermediate features, semantic priors, and diffusion trajectories with a gradient-norm adaptive loss weighting, enabling a lightweight student to absorb high-capacity teacher knowledge.
mainPoints.point: Adaptive multi-granularity distillation bridges the capacity gap.

oneSentenceSummary: Moebius is a 0.22B-parameter image inpainting framework that achieves 10B-level quality with over 15× inference speedup, using a novel Local-λ Mix Interaction block and adaptive multi-granularity distillation.
summary: Moebius is a lightweight image inpainting framework from HUST and VIVO AI Lab, compressing a 10B-level diffusion model into 0.22B parameters (less than 2% of FLUX.1-Fill-Dev) while matching or surpassing its generation quality across six benchmarks including natural scenes (Places2) and portraits (CelebA-HQ, FFHQ). The key innovation is the Local-λ Mix Interaction (LλMI) block, which reformulates self- and cross-attention by condensing spatial and semantic contexts into fixed-size matrices, bypassing quadratic complexity. This is paired with an adaptive multi-granularity distillation strategy operating entirely in latent space to align the compact student with the high-capacity teacher (PixelHacker). Moebius achieves 26 ms per step inference, a total of 15× acceleration, and sets a new efficiency standard for real-world inpainting. The project page includes extensive visual comparisons and accepts user uploads for testing.
